content: 1. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to reduce the rifabutin dose by up to 75% (e.g., 150 mg every other day or three times per week) and monitor closely for adverse effects. 2. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with cobicistat, reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg orally every other day and monitor for rifabutin-associated neutropenia and uveitis. 3. Rifampin significantly decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic failure. 4. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 6. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. When initiating riociguat in patients receiving atazanavir, reduce the riociguat dose to 5 mg three times daily and monitor closely. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir also increases ripretinib levels, and co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse reactions. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by these enzymes may be necessary. Monitor closely for side effects. 10. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to the increased risk of bleeding. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 13. Atazanavir increases the levels of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. Use alternative drugs or monitor closely. 14. Atazanavir increases the levels of ropivacaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 15. Atazanavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. 16. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day to reduce the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Use alternatives if available. 17. Rucaparib increases the levels of cobicistat and atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor closely. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID in patients with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 19. Atazanavir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 20. Atazanavir increases the levels of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels of selexipag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when co-administered with ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibitors. 23. Atazanavir increases the levels of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the selpercatinib dose and monitor for side effects. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 24. Atazanavir increases the levels of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage and monitor closely. 25. Atazanavir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect and monitor closely during co-administration. 26. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Chronic use of sildenafil for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is contraindicated. For erectile dysfunction, do not exceed 25 mg every 48 hours. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 29. Atazanavir increases the levels of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 30. Atazanavir increases the levels of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Atazanavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin by mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. 32. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use alternative drugs. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 33. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use alternative drugs. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 34. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate and monitor closely. 35. Atazanavir increases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
